analysis:
Changed region is only evictOldestEntry in SSDPrefixCache.swift (base 1772-1786, head 1772-1777). The inline victim loop is replaced with a call to SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest(index:), which takes a retire closure that still goes through retireIndexedEntries([url]). That wrapper keeps the removalLock, the hasSafeRoot and ownsEvictionRoot guards, and the externalChange reconciliation. The caller keeps the guard hasSafeRoot early return and still counts one eviction when freed > 0. The same safe-path deletion, removeItemIfSafe under the root, therefore runs on the same index-derived HMAC tag URLs. No new attacker-controlled path input and no change to crypto, TTL, tag derivation or the salt-scoping surfaces named in T-041. I read the rest of the visible file (donate, stage, readWindowSidecars) as unchanged context and saw no regression there.

Open integration questions: the new SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest implementation is outside the supplied evidence. It would need to preserve the old behavior: keep going past valid but undeletable victims, drop invalid or missing entries without touching their pathname, stop when externalChange is reported, and return only indexedBytesFreed. The old code returned 0 on externalChange, and the new code relies on the helper to do the same. The old semantics where retired.externalChange stops iteration can only be confirmed by reviewing that helper and its call-site closure semantics, which may affect T-041 disk-budget enforcement and availability. The closure accesses self.retireIndexedEntries without an explicit self capture, which should be benign if the closure is non-escaping.
